facts.fact_text: On 12 October 2006, Mr M., a leader of a human rights association called 'Mashr' based in Nazran, the Republic of Ingushetia, submitted a notification of a planned stationary demonstration (picket) to the authorities.
The planned picket was to be held on 16 October 2006 from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. near the monument to the heroes of the Second World War on Bazorkina Avenue in Nazran, the Republic of Ingushetia.
The purpose of the planned picket was to commemorate the journalist Anna Politkovskaya, who was murdered on 7 October 2006.
From 12 October 2006, the human rights association Mashr began to circulate information on the planned picket to prospective participants, including the applicants.
On 16 October 2006, before 4 p.m., the applicants arrived at the site of the planned picket near the monument to the heroes of the Second World War on Bazorkina Avenue in Nazran.
On 16 October 2006, Mr M. and others had also gathered at the site of the planned picket with the view to participating in it.
On 15 October 2006, the director of the human rights association Mashr received a handwritten letter from the Head of Nazran City Administration banning the planned picket.
The Head of Nazran City Administration banned the planned picket on the grounds that Mashr, being a non-commercial organisation, had no right to organise it.
On 16 October 2006, the police and the men in civilian clothes ordered the picketers, including the applicants, to disperse.
On 16 October 2006, the third, fourth and fifth applicants were apprehended on their way to their car after leaving the site of the planned picket.
On 16 October 2006, the sixth applicant was arrested at the site of the planned picket.
At approximately 4 p.m. on 16 October 2006, the third, fourth, fifth and sixth applicants were transferred to the Nazran police department.

As submitted by the applicants, when leaving the site of the planned picket on 16 October 2006, the second applicant was attacked from behind by two men.
During the fight that followed the attack on the second applicant, a man in civilian clothes named Mr T. hit the first applicant in her face.

In their challenge before the Nazran Town Court on 26 February 2007, the applicants submitted that the attacks on the first and the second applicant had taken place in the presence of some high-ranking police officers who tolerated the assaults.
The Justice of the Peace of the 9th Court Circuit of the Nasyr-Kortskiy District of Nazran examined a video recording which confirmed that Mr T. had punched the first applicant in the face.

The description of the video recording provided in the sentence of the Justice of the Peace of the 9th Court Circuit of the Nasyr-Kortskiy District of Nazran further stated that Mr T. had been prevented from hitting the first applicant for the second time by the policemen and the persons dressed in plain clothes present at the site.
